transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-20 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Lina (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Priya (Emberly Head of Security), Tom (Emberly Infra), Sofia (Emberly Compliance)

Summary: Kickoff for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 posture onboarding. Covered trust center access, controls mapping, RBAC/SSO, KMS/encryption approach and audit log exports. Agreed next steps and owners.

[00:00] Lina: Okay hi everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Lina with Redwood, account lead on your account. Marcus is our solutions engineer, he'll walk through the Trust Center and the technical pieces. Priya, Sofia, Tom — thanks for making time.
[00:18] Priya: Thanks Lina. We're mostly here to understand the evidence flow and make sure we can get the paperwork for our audit team, and then the technical bits — SSO, KMS, residency — those are big for us.
[00:30] Marcus: Great. My goal today is to show how we expose SOC 2/ISO artifacts in the Trust Center, discuss RBAC roles for least privilege, and then dig into KMS integration patterns. I'll also outline audit log formats and retention.
[00:45] Sofia: Quick ask on scope — Emberly's retail stack is multi-region, but legal needs EU data residency for PII. We'll need to map that in the controls.
[00:58] Marcus: Totally. We support region pinning for both hosted endpoints and for audit/log residency. We'll discuss the options — hosted with region restrictions, or Dedicated/Private if you need physical separation.
[01:15] Tom: Clarify Dedicated vs Private — Dedicated is reserved capacity on Redwood cloud, right? Private is VPC or on-prem with customer-managed networking?
[01:30] Lina: Exactly. Dedicated gives you tenant isolation on our infra with commit pricing; Private gives you a customer-managed control plane and optional on-prem packages. For compliance, Private is usually chosen when there's strict data residency or air-gap demands.
[01:45] Priya: For our auditors, we need SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 scope documents, plus evidence access. How do we get those?
[01:56] Marcus: We publish the SOC 2 report and the ISO summary in the Trust Center. There's a secure download flow. We can also provision role-based access so only your compliance team can see the artifacts. The Trust Center also has a controls-mapping spreadsheet that maps Redwood controls to common frameworks — we'll share that.
[02:15] Sofia: Is the mapping editable or is it a static mapping? Our internal control IDs need to be linked.
[02:24] Marcus: It's a spreadsheet export; we can add a column for your internal control IDs. We can also schedule a short mapping session to walk through each control and note any gaps.
[02:40] Priya: Okay. On KMS — we have a managed key policy through our cloud KMS. We prefer customer-managed keys for logs and model artifacts. How does Redwood integrate?
[02:52] Marcus: Redwood supports both: customer-managed keys via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for encrypting persistent storage and optional envelope encryption. For transit we use TLS, and you can bring your own key for at-rest encryption of model caches and snapshot artifacts. Small caveat: some internal ephemeral caches (KV cache) are encrypted by service keys but we can configure how long they persist.
[03:15] Tom: You said KV cache, uh — what's persisted where? I need the specifics for the auditors.
[03:25] Marcus: Sure, sorry — our runtime uses an in-memory KV cache for tokens, but we also persist certain checkpoint artifacts to object storage. For Private deployments we can configure the storage bucket to be your own, with customer-managed keys, so artifacts never land on Redwood-managed storage.
[03:45] Sofia: That would be preferable. Also want to confirm audit logs — are they streamed? What fields are included?
[03:54] Marcus: We can stream audit logs via syslog or push to S3/GCS with an object prefix. The logs include request id, timestamp, model name and version, route, token counts, calling principal (user/API key), region, and decision path for routing (if fallback occurred). Some PII fields are redacted — we do not store raw prompts by default unless you opt-in for debugging.
[04:20] Priya: Redaction is important. Can we request full logs with prompts for a limited retention window for incident response?
[04:29] Marcus: Yes — we have an elevated-access process. You request per-case access and we can export forensic logs for a defined window. Those exports can be encrypted with your KMS key.
[04:40] Tom: About SSO — we use Okta with SCIM. How does user provisioning and RBAC work in Redwood?
[04:48] Marcus: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. Roles are mapped from groups in Okta to Redwood roles — Admin, Audit-Only, Developer, Read-Only, etc. You can create custom roles too. We recommend Audit-Only for your compliance users.
[05:05] Priya: Are there built-in audit roles for Trust Center download only?
[05:09] Lina: Yes, there's a Trust Center Reader role; it only allows artifact access and metadata, not runtime or billing controls.
[05:16] Sofia: Sounds good. How do you handle evidence delivery for a Type II audit — is there a portal or do you email packages?
[05:26] Marcus: The Trust Center has a secure evidence portal. For Type II audits we can create a time-limited access token for auditors to pull artifacts. Alternatively, we can push a compiled evidence package to a customer bucket with customer-managed keys.
[05:40] Priya: Good. On controls mapping — what are the typical gaps customers see when going from our in-house stack to Redwood?
[05:49] Marcus: Common items: data residency mapping when customers are multi-region, proof-of-key-management for ephemeral caches, and integration of our deployment controls into customer change management processes. We also see adjustments around logging retention and ensuring SLA evidence is captured.
[06:05] Tom: Any guidance on retention windows? Our policy is 13 months for logs with 7 years for compliance-critical artifacts.
[06:12] Marcus: We typically offer configurable retention. Hosted by default is 90 days for verbose logs, but you can configure export/archival to your bucket for long-term retention. For Private deployments, you control retention entirely.
[06:30] Sofia: We need to map that in the control matrix.
[06:34] Lina: We'll get you the control mapping export so your team can annotate retention columns.
[06:40] [10-minute mark catch-up removed for brevity]
[10:05] Priya: A question on pen testing — do you share results or a snapshot of your vulnerability management?
[10:12] Marcus: We share an executive summary of pen tests and a vulnerability management policy in the Trust Center. Full reports are typically shared under NDA; we can coordinate that.
[10:24] Priya: We'll likely need the full report under NDA — auditors will ask.
[10:30] Lina: Noted, we'll add that as a deliverable.
[10:36] Tom: For the Trust Center access, how granular can access be? We have multiple teams: infra, audits, product.
[10:44] Marcus: Granular. You can create multiple roles and scoped tokens, and you can require MFA for artifact downloads. The UI supports folder-level permissions for evidence bundles.
[10:56] Sofia: That helps. Also need to know how Redwood shows model lineage — if we pin a model version for canary, is that recordable for auditors?
[11:06] Marcus: Yes — model versioning and rollout history are logged. The rollout events include who triggered the change, timestamp, source (api/console), and old/new model versions. That feeds into the audit trail.
[11:20] Priya: Great. Slight tangent — are there default retention labels on rollout events?
[11:26] Marcus: Audit events follow the same retention config; we can export them to your archival store.
[11:32] Lina: Quick check — anyone on the call needs a demo of the Trust Center live now or is a follow-up demo better?
[11:41] Tom: Follow-up is fine. We want to get our internal list of evidence types ready first.
[11:46] Priya: Agree.
[11:48] Marcus: Okay we'll plan a separate technical deep dive where we can demo the Trust Center and the KMS flow. That would be a 60–90 minute session.
[12:00] [15:00 timestamp jump—transcript continues]
[15:05] Priya: On encryption key rotation — how often do you rotate service keys, and what is the process for customer-managed keys?
[15:15] Marcus: Service keys rotate on a rolling schedule and there's an internal key management policy. For customer-managed keys, rotation is controlled by you; we support key versioning. Access to old artifacts encrypted with old keys is preserved via key metadata, but if you destroy a key you'll lose access.
[15:34] Tom: We will not destroy keys. We need to document key owners.
[15:38] Sofia: Also, does Redwood provide a KMS key usage audit? We want to show who accessed keys.
[15:44] Marcus: Your KMS provider will have key usage logs (e.g., CloudTrail). Redwood surfaces a record of actions that required key usage in the audit events, and that maps back to the KMS usage entries.
[15:58] Priya: Good. On compliance attestations — what is the ISMS scope for ISO 27001? Is it global or specific services?
[16:10] Marcus: Our ISO certification covers the hosted inference platform and the control plane services listed in the scope document in the Trust Center. Private deployments are covered for the control plane components we operate; customer-managed infrastructure is in scope only to the extent we operate it. We'll share the scope doc.
[16:30] Lina: I'll attach the ISO scope in the follow-up email.
[16:36] Tom: For evidence packaging, auditors want chain-of-custody for artifacts. How do you maintain integrity of artifact packages?
[16:44] Marcus: We provide checksums and can sign packages. When we push evidence to a customer bucket we include a signed manifest. If auditors need, we can sign with our code signing cert under NDA.
[16:58] Priya: Excellent.
[17:02] Marcus: Quick callout — some customers conflate request payload logging with metadata. Redwood's standard is to log metadata only; payloads are opt-in and governed by a separate retention & consent process. We'll need your policy decision whether you want prompts preserved for debugging.
[17:22] Sofia: We'll start with opt-out. If we need prompts for specific incidents we'll follow the elevated-access process.
[17:30] Lina: Noted.
[17:32] [22:00 mark omitted small discussion]
[22:15] Tom: On legal, will Redwood accept a data processing addendum with EU SCCs in place?
[22:23] Lina: Yes, we have a standard DPA that includes EU SCCs and can incorporate additional terms via an amendment. We can route legal to legal.
[22:34] Priya: We'll send our DPA checklist.
[22:37] Marcus: One more technical note — for Private deployments we can enable VPC peering and customer-controlled routing; this helps with egress control if you have strict residency.
[22:50] Tom: Good. Could we see a network diagram?
[22:54] Marcus: Yes, we'll include an architectural diagram for Private and Dedicated options in the package.
[23:03] Priya: Any limitations on log formats or naming? Our SIEM expects specific fields.
[23:10] Marcus: We'll provide a log schema mapping. The schema is JSON lines with standard fields; we can add customer-specific fields if needed. We'll also provide sample log files for ingestion testing.
[23:28] Sofia: Perfect.
[23:31] [30-minute mark capture — progress and recaps]
[30:05] Lina: Recap — Marcus will provision Trust Center access and share SOC/ISO docs; we'll send the control mapping spreadsheet; Emberly will compile the evidence list and residency constraints. Marcus will schedule the technical deep dive.
[30:26] Marcus: For scheduling, what's your availability next week?
[30:30] Tom: Tue/Wed mornings are good.
[30:34] Lina: We'll propose Wed 09:00 UTC for the technical session.
[30:38] Priya: Works for me.
[30:40] Marcus: Great.
[30:42] [40-minute mark — technical clarifications]
[40:05] Tom: One last question — if we need to run a proof-of-concept with sample traffic to validate latencies under EU routing, how quickly can Redwood spin up a test instance?
[40:18] Marcus: For hosted test instances we can provision a region-pinned deployment in 24–48 hours. For Dedicated/Private, provisioning is longer — typically a week to provision the environment and keys.
[40:33] Tom: 24–48 hours is fine for the POC. We'll plan to test with synthetic traffic and our SIEM ingestion.
[40:40] Priya: Will Redwood sign an MSA addendum for the POC?
[40:45] Lina: We have standard POC terms; I'll draft and share the MSA addendum.
[40:50] Marcus: I'll also share a checklist for evidence types you should collect while the POC runs.
[40:56] Sofia: That will help.
[41:00] [50-minute mark — closing]
[50:05] Lina: Any other questions?
[50:08] Priya: Not at the moment. Thanks, this was helpful.
[50:12] Tom: No.
[50:14] Sofia: Thanks.
[50:15] Lina: Okay we'll follow up with the SOC 2 and ISO docs, Trust Center invite, and a calendar invite for the technical deep dive on Wed 09:00 UTC. Action owners are in the notes.
[50:28] Marcus: Thanks everyone.
[50:30] Priya: Thanks.
[50:31] [call ends]
